mise.definition:
n. The issue in a writ of right.
n. Expense; cost; disbursement.
n. A tax or tallage; in Wales, an honorary gift of the people to
   a new king or prince of Wales; also, a tribute paid, in the country
   palatine of Chester, England, at the change of the owner of the
   earldom.
mise.translation:
n. 协定
[法] 争论点, 协定, 协约

mise en abyme.translation: [网络] 层结构；套层密藏；连环计

mise en place.translation: [网络] 赛前工作准备；餐前准备；准备工作

mise en scene.translation: <法> 舞台演出,舞台调度,周围环境

mise-en-scene.translation: n. <法>舞台的布景、道具等，舞台布置； <喻>事件的背景或环境

misease.definition: n. Want of ease; discomfort; misery.
misease.translation: n. 不安, 苦恼, 焦虑; 痛苦；苦难; 贫困, 贫穷

miseased.definition: a. Having discomfort or misery; troubled.
miseased.translation: n. [古语]不安, 苦恼, 焦虑；[古语]痛苦；苦难

miseducate.definition: v. t. To educate in a wrong manner.
miseducate.translation: vt.给…错误 ( 或有害 ) 的教育,教坏

miseducated.definition:
past participle of miseducate
v. t. To educate in a wrong manner.
miseducated.translation: (miseducate 的过去分词) vt.给…错误 ( 或有害 ) 的教育,教坏

miseducating.definition:
-ing form of miseducate
v. t. To educate in a wrong manner.
miseducating.translation: (miseducate 的现在分词) vt.给…错误 ( 或有害 ) 的教育,教坏

misemphasis.translation: n. 错误的强调(或侧重)

misemploy.definition:
v. t. To employ amiss; as, to misemploy time, advantages,
   talents, etc.
misemploy.translation: v. 误用, 应用不当

misentry.definition: n. An erroneous entry or charge, as of an account.
misentry.translation: [计] 错误输入, 不准确引入

miser.definition: n. a stingy hoarder of money and possessions (often living miserably)
miser.translation: n. 守财奴, 吝啬鬼, (石油工程上用的)锥钻头

miserable.definition:
s. very unhappy; full of misery
s. characterized by physical misery
miserable.translation: a. 悲惨的；痛苦的；卑鄙的

miserableness.definition: n. The state or quality of being miserable.
miserableness.translation: 痛苦, 悲惨, 可怜

miserables.translation:
a. 不幸的, 悲惨的, 可悲的, 可叹的；(人)痛苦的, 苦恼的, 流露痛苦的
n. 遭受苦难的人；不幸的人；极度贫困的人

miserablism.translation: 愁苦主义(通过绘画反映作者本身痛苦经历和社会不幸)

miserably.translation: adv. 非常不幸地, 可悲地, 贫困地

miserere.definition:
n. The psalm usually appointed for penitential acts, being
   the 50th psalm in the Latin version. It commences with the word
   miserere.
n. A musical composition adapted to the 50th psalm.
n. A small projecting boss or bracket, on the under side of
   the hinged seat of a church stall (see Stall). It was intended, the
   seat being turned up, to give some support to a worshiper when
   standing. Called also misericordia.
n. Same as Ileus.
miserere.translation: n. 求主祈怜之祷告或其乐曲, 恳求之声

misericord.translation: n. 一种短剑, 凳下方的横木, 免戒室

misericorde.definition:
n. Compassion; pity; mercy.
n. Same as Misericordia, 2.

misericords.translation: (misericord 的复数) n.一种短剑, 凳下方的横木, 免戒室

miseries.translation: n. 痛苦( misery的名词复数 ); 痛苦的事; 穷困; 常发牢骚的人

miserliness.definition: n. total lack of generosity with money

miserly.definition: s (used of persons or behavior) characterized by or indicative of lack of generosity
miserly.translation: a. 吝啬的, 贪婪的

misers.definition: n. a stingy hoarder of money and possessions (often living miserably)
misers.translation: n. 守财奴, 吝啬鬼( miser的复数形式 )

misery.definition:
n. a state of ill-being due to affliction or misfortune
n. a feeling of intense unhappiness
misery.translation: n. 痛苦, 悲惨, 不幸, 穷困

misesteem.translation:
vt. 轻视, 不予尊重
n. 轻视

misestimate.definition:
v judge incorrectly
v calculate incorrectly

misestimation.translation: n. misestimate（误估，误算；错误评价）的变形
